#4032. 6 Hints That Korra Didn't Ruin the World in Avatar: Seven Havens

Shayna Josi is a Features Writer from South Africa. She is a ghostwriter, copywriter, and editor in the publishing industry.

The Legend of Korra never received the same acclaim that Avatar: The Last Airbender did, but most of its seasons reach the same heights and even beyond. Korra is one of my favorite characters, period. The release of Avatar Seven Havens has reignited parts of the fandom who have always hated her, and brought back debates that should have ended ten years ago.

Compared to previous series from the Avatar franchise, the world of Avatar: Seven Havens has changed rather dramatically.

There’s a lot of reason to suspect that not everything is as it seems in Avatar Seven Havens, and this is expressed in a lot of ways. There’s more going on here than what’s on the surface, and I wouldn’t be surprised if it’s revealed that Korra is just a convenient scapegoat for a disaster caused by someone else. I’m not just pulling this assertion out of nowhere, and there’s a lot of evidence in Seven Havens to back it up.

We don’t know why the Cataclysm happened, but evidence points towards some kind of Chernobyl disaster involving Future Industries and Varrick. While the evidence currently points to Asami, recent information released by Paramount+ that mentions Varrick makes me suspicious of him, and it wouldn’t be outside the realm of reality that he reached too far considering he already made a weapon of mass destruction using spirit vines.

The spirit vines seem to be the key here, as well as the spirit portal inside Republic City. It’s likely that spirit energy was harnessed, then something went terribly wrong. Korra’s involvement appears to be limited to trying to contain the threat, and she may have reduced the Cataclysm from an event that ended all life to one that only took out most of the world’s population.

Pavi and Nisha’s visions of Korra definitely do not tell the whole story, and the fact that there’s an obvious timeskip between their versions of Korra makes it more obvious that information is being hidden from us to create a misleading narrative.

Pavi sees Korra looking sadly at Republic City, where we then jump to Nisha’s vision, which shows Korra destroying pipes that release energy. Korra is wearing a different outfit in each of these visions, implying they take place at different times. It also contrasts with the Korra we know, who is seen in the Old World mover and who Nisha realizes doesn’t look like the monster they’ve been taught to see her as. These are important details that form a picture that tells us there is more going on. What happened in that gap is key, and will likely be the final piece of the puzzle.

Fans have pointed out the similarities between the version of Korra destroying the pipes and Korra’s PTSD vision from LoK season 4. What the vision exactly was has never been confirmed, but it’s likely a representation of her state of mind and a manifestation of her PTSD and mental state. In practical terms, it could have also been a dark spirit drawn to Korra’s pain, as the spirit that leads her to the swamp can also see it.

If this is the case, then a spirit mimicking Korra has a precedent, and could be happening here. Considering she’s wearing a different outfit and missing her betrothal necklace when she’s destroying the pipes, it’s possible that this is a dark spirit rather than Korra. We still don’t have the whole picture, but there could be a reason to explain why a spirit would do this, especially if Vaatu is somehow involved.

Avatar: Seven Havens has showcased many connections to the past so far. These are some of the best connections.

Korra was hot-headed and impulsive in season one of LoK, and this version of her may have done something to inadvertently destroy the world. But to think that she did post-season four is completely out of character for her. When we first meet her, Korra is headstrong, impatient, and convinced that she can solve most problems through direct confrontation. However, her experiences gradually teach her that being the Avatar requires more than strength. She learns patience, humility, and how to understand people whose perspectives differ from her own. Korra learns to recognise her limitations and accept that not every problem can be solved by fighting harder.

That doesn't mean Korra could never make another terrible mistake, but it would be out of character for her to be manipulated like she was by Unalaq in season two. It would be a massive regression of her development. Any explanation of the Cataclysm needs to account for that growth rather than simply assuming she reverted to her most impulsive tendencies.

It’s important to consider how much of Korra's reputation comes from what actually happened and how much comes from the way history has remembered her. Seven Havens takes place more than two centuries after LoK, which is plenty of time for history to be lost.

“She wasn’t a hero or a villain. She was a person, and she was complex. She had depth to her. She is someone who, just like any other Avatar, and like many other Avatars before her, potentially did something that failed the world, or maybe she did something that was completely seen differently than years later.” - Sehaj Sethi, Avatar Seven Havens executive producer.

It’s clear that something terrible did happen, and that Korra was likely involved, but that doesn’t mean her actions, deliberate or otherwise, led to the Cataclysm. The Avatar would be a convenient scapegoat as they’re incredibly powerful and have a prominent role in global events, but the series as a whole has made it clear that you don’t need to be the Avatar to change the world in terrible ways with Sozin, Kuvira, Zaheer, and Tagah as just some examples.

One of the main themes that Seven Havens is tackling is clearly about propaganda, misinformation, and misdirection. This is shown in so many parts of Seven Havens, especially through its characters. Several major characters are a part of the White Lotus and lie to their friends and loved ones. Karthik says, “You know why people think they should know the truth? They believe it’ll keep them safe. Funny. Usually the opposite is true.” The Faceless kidnap benders, but it’s revealed that the kidnapped benders willingly joined them. Agam, the closest character the show has to a villain, deceived everyone with a fake identity.

The children's play on Avatar Day in episode one depicted Korra in a very similar way to the Fire Nation’s depictions of Aang in ATLA. There are too many things off here for there not to be something going on. There’s not a lot of information about what happened to cause the Cataclysm, and the evidence based on the themes of Seven Havens indicates that there’s more to the story.

In Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game, there are Future Characters We Want to See like Jet, Hama, and Roku.

#4031. Diablo 4’s Warlock looks like an unhinged Necromancer with Sorcerer energy in first look at gameplay

Diablo 4's practitioner of forbidden arts, The Warlock, has been officially unveiled as the second class coming with Lord of Hatred.

Thanks to a meaty, well-produced Diablo 4 Developer Update, we got to have our promised first look at gameplay of the Warlock, the second of two classes coming to the game with the upcoming Lord of Hatred expansion.

The showcase offered a deep look at the Warlock’s core archetypes, its gameplay and skills loop, and where the class sits within the game’s existing roster of diverse classes.

Since the initial reveal of Lord of Hatred, The Warlock has remained the mysterious second class. Anyone who pre-purchased the expansion was able to get immediate access to The Paladin, the other class arriving with the expansion. It wasn’t until February that Blizzard officially revealed the class to the world, but we had to wait until this most recent Developer Update to actually see it in action.

The Warlock’s pragmatism exists as the counterpart to The Paladin's purity, in that Warlocks don’t shy away from harnessing the powers of Hell to eliminate their enemies. The class can conjure up demons to do their bidding, and utilise attacks previously only available to legions of Hell.

The Warlock is a hybrid pet and caster class. Their gameplay revolves around summoning demons, and undermining enemies with shadow arts. They rely on two resources: Wrath, and Dominance. Casting Skills consumes Wrath, whereas Dominance is what allows the Warlock to summon and exploit demons.

The Warlock has four archetypes players can spec into. Legions are traditional summoners who rely on overwhelming numbers to crush enemies. Vanguards are closer to Sorcerers, capable of dealing damage head-on. Masterminds utilise shadowcraft to slowly drain their enemies. Finally, Ritualists are summoners of the most terrifying Hell demons.

The Warlock is able to do this by fusing Soul Shards into their bodies. Going down any of the four paths becomes available after reaching level 30, which is when the class mechanic is unlocked. Each Soul Shard is tied to a certain demon, and its through that power that the Warlock is able to call upon them in combat. Your choice does, of course, affect your abilities going forward.

Warlocks arrive alongside new Uniques that cater to their specific playstyles, which is similar to what we’ve previously seen with The Paladin, and The Spiritborn before that.

Lord of Hatred arrives April 28. While we wait, Diablo 4’s next season is kicking off next week to deliver a bit of mindless fun to hold us over until the big day.

#4030. Grand Theft Auto VI Shatters Records, Making $3.79 Billion In 24 Hours As The Biggest Entertainment Launch Ever

Grand Theft Auto VI dropped yesterday to massive success, and while we expected it to do well, hearing the numbers behind the historic launch day is still staggering. According to a statement obtained by Bloomberg's Jason Schreier and IGN, Rockstar has confirmed that the open-world juggernaut made $3.79 billion in 24 hours. This makes it not just the biggest video game launch of all time – it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, and it's not especially close.

Schreier goes on to confirm that much of that money comes from GTA VI's record-breaking pre-orders. It turns out, there were 32.5 million pre-sales, which is a truly mind-bending number. For context, its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, currently the second best-selling game of all time, sold 11.21 million copies in the first 24 hours – GTAVI nearly triples that figure. In pre-orders alone, the game has become the 30th best-selling game of all time, with more copies sold in the first day than Elden Ring and Super Mario Odyssey have sold, period.

In terms of the dollar amount, GTAVI's $3.79 billion in 24 hours is not just more money than any film has made in its opening weekend; it's more money than any movie has ever made in the box office – even Avengers: Endgame, which currently holds the highest worldwide gross, is still shy of $3 billion after several successful theatrical runs.

Grand Theft Auto VI also set the record on Metacritic for the highest-reviewed game of all time (with an average critic score of 99), and it headlined this week's rollout of the Game Awards 2026 nominees, with more nominations than any other game. We also loved it, and our editor-in-chief Matt Miller scored it a perfect 10.

#4029. Marathon launch player numbers are about half those of the Server Slam, at least on PC

Marathon hasn't quite been able to attract the same volume of players the recent Server Slam did.

After a couple of delays, a plagiarism lawsuit, and at least one internal reboot, Bungie’s next big game has officially launched. Marathon, the extraction shooter from the studio behind Destiny, has managed to find a decent, if a little small of an audience.

The game’s player numbers on Steam are being compared to its recent free, open weekend, and not in a favourable manner.

Prior to Marathon’s launch, Bungie held a multi-day Server Slam, which offered anyone interested in playing the game a chance to try out almost all of its classes, two of its maps, as well as many of its gameplay and progression systems.

The open test was largely well-received, and players actually showed up for it. It peaked at a very respectable 143,621 concurrent players on Steam, which put it within striking distance of the peak concurrent of its chief competitor, Arc Raiders - at least when you compare both of their pre-launch Server Slam events.

In Arc Raiders’ case, those figures were far outpaced at the game’s actual launch, and the Embark shooter continues to command a very active player base to this day. A paid product garnering far more players than the same product’s own free sampler is never not a good sign, so many hoped something similar would happen with Marathon.

Marathon has now officially launched, and it doesn’t look like it managed to pull an Arc Raiders - at least so far. At its peak, the Bungie shooter attracted 88,337 concurrent players on Steam (via SteamDB), which is a little over half of its Server Slam’s 143,621 peak concurrent.

Numbers have, of course, dropped since then, which is normal, as players log off for the night. This is obviously not the end of the road for Marathon. Friday, and the weekend, may well push numbers closer to the Server Slam heights.

Indeed, word of mouth is quite positive, with the game currently sitting at a Very Positive user review rating on Steam, based on over 4,600 reviews. As has been proven time and time again in recent years, nothing catapults a game like players emphatically advocating for it to their friends, so it could simply be that mainstream players are cautious.

It will become clear where things settle over the weekend.

#4028. Retailers Can’t Keep Up With PS5 Demand Following GTA 6's Launch

Six years after the PS5 launched, we're seeing people struggle to get their hands on one again. GTA 6 arrived on November 19, and with Christmas less than a month away, the console is proving increasingly difficult to find at its regular retail price.

The PlayStation 5 has officially exceeded 100 million units sold worldwide in its lifetime.

The timing couldn't be worse for Sony. AI companies are driving up demand for memory chips, putting pressure on console manufacturers. Now, millions of people want to play a game that's only available on the PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

The Washington Post reports that the PS5 Pro was already going out of stock in the US before GTA 6 launched. Resellers have been asking as much as $1,900 for a console that normally costs $900. In Japan, Sony's own store uses a lottery that requires a Japanese account with 60 hours of verified PS4 or PS5 playtime.

That might deter scalpers, but it also puts first-time PlayStation buyers at a disadvantage. If you're buying a PS5 specifically for GTA 6 and haven't played on a Sony console before, you won't qualify for the lottery.

It's not just the Pro that's hard to find, either. German publication GamesWirtschaft spoke to MediaMarkt-Saturn, which acknowledged that interest in GTA 6 had exacerbated the already high demand for consoles. The retailer expects more stock in December, though quantities will be limited. On Black Friday, the chain advertised 7,000 bundles containing a PS5 Digital Edition and a second controller for €657.98, available only at selected stores while stocks lasted. Xbox consoles have also been affected by the shortage.

Those of us who remember the first couple of years of the PS5's life will be familiar with the sight of consoles listed at ridiculous prices on resale sites. What's particularly frustrating this time around is that the PS5 isn't even new hardware anymore. Six years into a console generation, you'd normally be looking for Black Friday discounts, not paying a premium just to get one.

The PS5 had already passed 100 million shipments worldwide before GTA 6 came out, but the milestone came during a relatively slow year for hardware sales. Only 3.2 million PS5 units were shipped in the first half of Sony's 2026 fiscal year. Annual shipments peaked at 20.8 million in fiscal 2023. GTA 6 could give the PS5 a second wind at a particularly difficult time for console manufacturers.

In a PlayStation Blog post on November 23, the company revealed that 70% of newly connected PS5 consoles during GTA 6's opening days had Rockstar's game as the first title played on them.

Sony also recorded its highest single-day number of new PS5 connections outside the end-of-year holiday period since the hardware launched in 2020. More than 39 million people played GTA 6 on PS5 over its first four days, collectively spending 683 million hours in the game.

That follows Circana's launch-day report, which found that 61% of active US PS5 players were playing GTA 6. We covered those figures earlier this week, when Circana also reported that US PS5 players who launched GTA 6 spent an average of more than eight hours with the game running that day.

For those of us who primarily play on PC, there's an additional dilemma. GTA 6 still doesn't have a PC release date, and buying a console just to play one game is already an expensive proposition. It's a much harder purchase to justify if you're paying well above the recommended retail price.

GTA 6 still doesn't have a PC release date, and buying a console just to play one game is already an expensive proposition.

I'd rather wait for one of those December restocks than pay a scalper twice the retail price. As much as I've been looking forward to returning to Vice City, GTA 6 isn't going anywhere.

#4026. Review: Gamesir Nova Vision Controller For Switch 1 & 2 - Unique Features Elevate This Mid-Range Pad

Accessory developer Gamesir doesn’t often make controllers with the Switch 1 and 2 in mind, instead focusing primarily on Xbox and PC. So when it announced the new Nova Vision, my Spider-Sense tingled.

The latest entry in the mid-range Nova line, the Vision adds two unique features: a colour LCD screen for quick and easy customisation, and Hall Effect analogue sticks with adjustable tension without the need for extra tools. At $54.99, this is a compelling controller as it is, but Gamesir has also included a charging stand to ensure you’re always good to go.

The analogue sticks really are the star of the show. Featuring raised, textured edges with a grippy rubber material, they actually share much in common with the PS5 analogue sticks and feel great to use. The Hall Effect technology should keep stick drift at bay, while the transparent domes let you see into the interior – a neat little touch I personally liked. My wife wasn’t keen on it, so your own appreciation may vary.

Adjustable tension isn’t completely new — Gulikit’s TT Pro and Max controllers do the same thing — but this is the first instance I’ve tried a controller that lets you do it without any extra tools. All you need to do is twist the sticks anti-clockwise to loosen the tension, and clockwise to tighten.

At their loosest, the sticks feel light and floaty, good for open-world games like Breath of the Wild in which you need to move great distances. At their tightest, they allow for more precise movements, which might come in handy for racing games like Mario Kart World or first-person shooters like Modern Warfare 4.

Had it required an extra tool to adjust the tension, I might have just left the Nova Vision at one setting and been done with it. However, being able to simply twist the sticks to my desired tension at any point encouraged experimentation based on the game I’m playing. It’s a neat feature, and thankfully they take a fair bit of pressure to twist, so you’re never going to do it accidentally.

The screen acts as your main hub for functions and customisation. You might notice at first glance that the Vision is lacking buttons for Start, Select, and Home - they’re all housed in the screen. Click it on the bottom right for Start, the bottom left for Select, and anywhere near the top for Home.

Then you’ve got the ‘M’ button at the bottom, nestled in between the D-pad and right analogue stick. Hold this down for about five seconds to access the configuration menu. Here, you can select whether to connect to Switch, PC, or mobile, remap buttons to your liking, switch between profiles, adjust motion controls and vibration intensity, and more.

When you’re in the configuration menu, navigation is simple: use the D-pad to highlight menu items, ‘A’ to select, and ‘B’ to go back. When you’re done, just hold down the ‘M’ button again to exit. If you’re wondering where the capture button is, there isn’t one, but a quick double-tap of ‘M’ provides the same functionality. There’s no ‘C’ button for chat, mind you.

Inputs feel pretty good, overall. The D-pad, shoulder buttons, and back buttons are mechanical and provide a nice, satisfying click when pressed. The ABXY inputs, meanwhile, are membrane and considerably quieter by comparison. The main shoulder triggers can be swapped between full motion travel and short, clicky stops, so experiment with this to find your preference.

The back buttons aren’t mapped to anything by default. You can map any individual input to the buttons, or opt for any combo macro up to 12 inputs. They’re positioned nicely, allowing your middle fingers to rest comfortably, and they’re much quieter than some of the competition on the market.

Connection is done in three ways: Bluetooth, 2.4G wireless via a dongle, or a USB-C cable. The 1000mAh battery should comfortably last over 10 hours on a single charge, but if you’re using the included charging dock, you’ll likely never need to worry about this. The dock itself is pretty small and minimal in its design, with a nice, subtle RGB strip that slowly pulses when the controller is docked. And yes, it does feature wake-up support for Switch 2.

Finally, it’s worth mentioning that you can further customise the controller via the Gamesir Connect PC app, allowing you to add your own images and GIFs to the built-in screen. Unfortunately, the downside here is that it’s not compatible with Mac, so I’ve been unable to test this feature out myself.

For the mid-range price, the Nova Vision is an excellent controller for Switch 1 and 2. The built-in screen allows for quick customisation and remapping if needed, while the adjustable tension in the analogue sticks feels intuitive and genuinely useful for different games and genres. Add in Hall Effect technology and the charging dock, and you’re getting a lot of bang for your buck.

The lack of a ‘C’ button is a shame, while introducing Mac compatibility for the Gamesir Connect app would be an easy win. Furthermore, some folks just might not be keen on functions like Start and Home being accessed via the screen. If that’s you, then this probably isn’t for you. For everyone else, the Nova Vision is a solid choice.

#4024. Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

There's a new Nioh 3 patch out in the wild, and it's one that any player who regularly summons in boss fights will really appreciate.

Team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related issues.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

The more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

In the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

#4023. 8 PS1 JRPGs Where You’re Actually the Villain

Adam Braunstein is a dedicated gaming writer who has countless hours in the gaming world and a variety of genres experienced and conquered.

Being the hero is all the rage when it comes to videogames, but some like to play the greyer side of things and sometimes, you can find yourself playing the evil side of events and not even realize it until additional context in the game is given.

The JRPG genre has quite a few occurrences of this, where you may think you’re being benevolent all the while you’re actually the biggest threat of all. It’s an amazing rug pull that many games often refuse to even attempt and we’re thankful we’ve got one genre where it happens all the time.

The PS1 JRPG catalog is even better than many think.

We’re going to check out some of the instances on the PS1 where you take the role of a villain, whether you know it or not.

Right from the start of the game, the status of the main characters is a murky one at best. I mean, we’re playing as terrorists for god’s sake. And yeah, while we’re saving the planet and everything, we’re still committing atrocities in the name of doing so. I mean, did you think those Mako reactors had no workers in them?

If that’s not enough, Cloud gets fully possessed throughout the game to pretty much deliver the Black Materia, an essential doomsday device right into the hands of the big bad Sephiroth, which, guess what? Ends up completely dooming the planet (Don’t @ me Advent Children fam). He literally performs an action under his control or not, that ends up killing millions and millions of people. It’s not entirely his fault, but when millions get evaporated in an instant, I don’t think they’d care all that much knowing that Cloud was controlled against his will. He’s a terrorist whose actions led to essentially the end of life on a planet. Can’t be much worse than that.

Brigandine: The Legend of Forsena is one of the best and most interesting tactical JRPGs on the PS1 because it gives you control over entire armies, lets you customize them to your liking and throws you into battles that test every bit of your knowledge of the game. It’s like a grand scale chess match with hundreds of different pieces.

There are a bunch of countries to choose from here, and one of them is the “evil” Esgares Empire, which is about as close to the classic big bad empire of a JRPG as you're going to get here because this game colors in shades of grey rather than black and white. The cool part about playing as this empire in the game, is that you get the feeling that you’re finally behind the controls of one of those comically large armies that would throw hundreds of enemies at you in a JRPG. You’re now the final boss. And you get some interesting story context along the way that goes a long way in fleshing out the “villains” of the game into something that is a bit more understanable in this world full of war, backstabbing and betrayal.

SaGa Frontier is one of those games that you either get or you don’t get, but for the ones that get it, they absolutely love it, hence why it’s been a series that still goes till this day. I think the appeal is in how many characters you get to experience

One of those characters is Blue, and unlike a lot of JRPG protagonists, Blue doesn't have some particularly noble reason for going on his grand adventure. He’s a mage who ends up killing his twin brother all in the pursuit of power. Now, while most JRPG characters would have some kind of remorse or reluctance to doing this, Blue doesn’t. He doesn’t care one bit. He’s just a cold-blooded mage with a one-track mind, and anyone he picks up along the way is just a tool to him. A definite far cry from any hero I’ve seen and much closer to the villain than any actual villain in the game.

Xenogears is one of the most ambitious games of all time, and with that comes a twisting and turning story that has all kinds of amazing reveals and epic moments. One of those moments comes in Solaris, where the hero Fei, is revealed to also be Id, a character who until that point, has been the villain of the game, killing thousands, and being just an unstoppable force in the process.

The reveal is somewhat predictable, but still very impactful and clears up so much about the story. But because of the reveal, you also have to live with being a character who just murdered god knows how many people and is responsible for even the destruction and murder of many of Fei’s friends too. It’s a sobering moment, and a powerful one that makes you wonder who the real bad guy is in this story. As far as humans go? Fei is easily the villain in this story (Krellian and Ramsus are saints, and I’ll hear nothing more from you on the matter.)

If you like your JRPGs to constantly surprise you, here are 8 JRPGs that totally reinvent themselves halfway through.

Vanguard Bandits is on my Mount Rushmore of underappreciated games, and it’s because it was so ahead of its time in so many ways, from ggameplayto story, to character writing. It was such a unique gem of a game and one that put you in full control in a way no other JRPG had before then. That control comes from the choices that you make along the way. Some of which put you on a straight and narrow path, others turn the game into a complete clownshow,w which is definitely worth experiencing one time, and another puts you on the path of joining a supposedly evil empire.

You can turn your back on the merc band of do-gooders if you want here, and honestly, it’s a really compelling turn of the story if you do. Suddenly the characters you were desperately fighting against are now allies, and their motivations seem far more understandable when they’ve got your back in battle. It’s the best non-Gundam, anime-styled mech-based JRPG story you can find. That’s a niche I know, but for the ones who are into it, it’s as prime as it gets.

Final Fantasy IV really sets the stage for the type of path the series would soon embark upon. It’s really dark,k and that starts off apparent as you begin the game playing, as Cecil, a member of a militant group fresh off committing some absolutely deplorable acts in order to satisfy his masters. And it doesn’t get much better from there, especially when delivering a package to the village of Mist that ends up destroying it outright. This is your hero, folks, and you’re playing as them. Kain isn’t much better either, following in line like a good little soldier.

I’m all for redemption stories, but here, no matter how much Kain and Cecil eventually realize the folly of their ways, I don’t know if the dead bodies in their wake really care about their face turn. To me, these are the villains of the story fighting against a much larger, cosmic level of evil. But for the humans who are unaware of the greater dealings in the story? These two are absolutely terrible people, and no amount of character rehab changes that face for me.

Tactics Ogre has one of the most shocking choices that I've seen in a JRPG, which is saying a lot because there have been plenty of impactful ones over the years. What makes this one so interesting is because there isn’t a huge build to it, and it happens early on in the game.

You, playing as Denam, a young man caught up in a war, feels pretty much par for the course at the start of the game. You’re up against an evil empire, and it seems hopeless, and we’ve seen this type of story many times before. And you believe in everything you’re doing is for the betterment of your people. Well, that belief is tested when you’re asked to slaughter thousands of innocent people in order to basically create a false flag attack and get people to join your cause. The interesting thing is that you can choose whether to accept or refuse. If you accept, you’re essentially getting yourself on the bad path of the game, even though the game itself just calls the route the Law Route. It’s part of what makes the game so fascinating, because you see there are no real good sides here. It’s just the ugliness of war, in every way you can imagine.

Breath of Fire IV is one JRPG I need to be remade. It’s such a cool setup and It’s really a travesty that it’s one that seems to have been left behind by the gaming world. You play as Ryu, a mysterious young man with a classic case of “WTF is happening”-itis. And as he discovers his powers, you get a glimpse of another mysterious character named Fou Lou. Who is he? Where is he? And most importantly, when is he?

These answers and more come to forefront as you discover his story, and slowly realize that this ultra powerful character is the villain of the game, under your control. It’s the first time I really saw this in a game this blatantly at least. He’s such a compelling character too, that I almost preferred playing as him over our usual ragtag party that the Ryu segments have. You slowly get to know his motivations and why he hates humanity so much. Getting to know a villain this way is simply brilliant, and letting you experience that power, which you will soon one day have to overcome is a great way to show a player just how over their head they truly will be in when coming face to face with a character of this magnitude.

The bad guys of the 1990s were absolutely unmatched. Here are 8 PS1 JRPGs where the villain feels more compelling than the hero.

#4022. Deborah Ann Woll Will Reprise Her Role As Laufey In Amazon's God Of War Series

Deborah Ann Woll, likely best known as Karen Page in Daredevil and Daredevil: Born Again, has just been cast as Laufey in the upcoming live-action God of War series. It's a perfect fit, not just because she's a great actress – Woll already portrays the character in the video games.

The live-action God of War series is currently in production, and after a series of headlines about Kratos, it's refreshing to get some news about his late wife, Faye. Also known as Laufey, she dies right before 2018's God of War (which the show is based on) begins. The game centers on a journey between Kratos and his son to spread Faye's ashes from the highest peak in the realms.

Faye is not present in 2018's God of War, but she appears in God of War Ragnarök in flashback and dream sequences. In this game, she's played by Deborah Ann Woll, an oddly high-profile casting for a relatively minor character. It all made sense earlier this year, however, when we learned Woll will reprise her role as the star of God of War Laufey, which tells Faye's story as she fights through a mythological underworld.

It's a cool piece of news, and it implies that Faye will have more of a presence in the series than in the first game, where she never appears at all. As for what shape that presence takes, we have no idea.

Woll joins the likes of Alastair Duncan, who plays Mimir and will also reprise his role. The two don't really interact in the games, however, so it's unlikely to see them share the screen in the series.

The main news around Prime Video's God of War is about its protagonist. Originally announced as Ryan Hurst, the actor suffered a serious injury on the set of the show and was replaced by Dave Bautista (Guardians of the Galaxy, Glass Onion) in August. Other key cast members include Callum Vinson as Atreus, Sonya Walger as Freya, Mandy Patinkin as Odin, and Ed Skrein as Baldur.

For more God of War, you can look forward to Woll's portrayal of Faye in God of War Laufey, though it recently got delayed.

Update: Studio confirms lack of Xbox version

Update [Fri 27th Nov 2026, 3:38pm]: Developer Playtonic has now confirmed we won't be getting an Xbox version (at least at launch). We've shared their statement elsewhere on Pure Xbox:

News Yooka-Laylee Developer Issues Statement On Why Definitive Edition Is Skipping Xbox

"...just isn't viable for us at this time"

Original Story: Here's a strange one for you! The fantastic Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair has been one of the best platformers on Xbox since it launched back in 2019, but the game's new "Definitive Edition" appears to be skipping Series X and S.

A new announcement today revealed that the upgraded Definitive Edition will include enhanced visuals, up to 4K resolution at 120FPS, two orchestrated soundtracks and more, but it will only be available on PC, Switch 2 and PS5.

As you can imagine, that hasn't gone down well with Xbox fans.

The comments section of Playtonic Games' post is full of reactions like these, and at the time of writing, no response or statement has been provided for why the Definitive Edition isn't coming to Xbox in addition to other platforms.

There may well be a very good reason for it, and here's hoping we might get clarification at some point in the near future, but at least for the time being, it seems we're going to have to miss out on this new enhanced version.

As disappointing as this is, the 2019 original is still well worth playing if you're interested!

#4020. Gallery: Get A Closer Look At Nintendo's Playable Ocarina Of Time

Just last week, Nintendo announced that the upcoming playable and electric ocarinas, launching in conjunction with Ocarina of Time, will initially be sold on an invite-only basis in Europe. We still don't have a firm release date for either of them over here in the EU (and no invites have been sent out just yet, as far as we can see), but the good folks over at Nintendo have sent us a lovely playable model, so we can get a close-up look at it all the same.

So, we thought it would be only right to show you lovely lot what's in the box — it's always good to see it from a bunch of different angles before you decide whether to pick one up for yourself, after all. Below, we've done exactly that.

The ocarina itself is naturally the star of the show, with Nintendo putting together a pretty decent likeness to the instrument seen in the game. Sure, the blue is a little different and the overall shape is a little thinner, but it still cuts a pretty iconic silhouette.

The box also contains a neat little wrist strap, so you can rock out on your ocarina without worrying about it slipping out of your hands from all the raw musical talent.

Overall, it's a nice bit of kit. The plastic is certainly on the thinner side for the £29.99 price tag (a nice ceramic option this ain't), but it looks the part on display.

#4019. One Of Our Favorite Action Games From Gamescom, Showa American Story, Has Been Delayed To 2027

Showa American Story is set in a world where Japan's 1980s economic prowess was strong enough to purchase America, and so it did. Taking place in Neo Yokohama, formerly Hollywood, this raunchy, zany action game was one of our favorites at Gamescom 2026, but unfortunately, we'll have to wait a little longer than expected to experience more of this adventure.

That's because developer Nekcom Entertainment and publisher 4Divinity have revealed that Showa American Story has been delayed to next year. Originally due out sometime this year (though it became clear that wasn't going to happen given the radio silence as we near the year's end), Showa American Story will now launch on PlayStation 5 and PC on October 28, 2027.

"Reaching this milestone after five years of development means a lot to our entire team," the studio writes in a statement. "With core game content now complete, we're dedicating our full focus to polishing and optimizing the experience so that when you step into Showa American Story, it feels cohesive, responsive, and complete. Thank you for your continued support, enthusiasm, and patience along the way. We can't wait to welcome you on October 28, 2027."

In the meantime, read Game Informer's Showa American Story hands-on preview from this year's Gamescom. After that, check out our list of the top 10 action games to play right now.

#4018. The Sims 4 patch makes it so your public lot gatherings won't be interrupted by rogue Sims

Stranger Sims will no longer just crash your public lot events in The Sims 4 to talk about whatever.

The Sims 4 will soon get a new update to resolve a number of issues, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most important is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

Speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis said this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in new saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a new lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an update that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently announced that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

#4015. Ubisoft Wants Rayman To Become A Huge, Transmedia Star

Ubisoft is gearing up to launch Rayman Legends Retold, a reimagined remake of the 2013 original. While many have questioned the decision to remake a game that arguably still looks and plays great to this day, the developers have been clear in their intention to use Retold as a launchpad for the future of the franchise.

Now, in a new interview with The Game Business, brand producer Loïc Gounon has expressed much broader ambitions for the character, perhaps bringing Rayman more in line with something like Sonic in terms of visibility.

In other words, Gounon is thinking about not only games, but other mediums too, including TV shows and comics. The first step is to ensure the brand's success in regions such as the US and Asia, with previous Rayman titles' success being largely limited to Europe.

“I would like to see Rayman as a must-have IP for video games across the world. Rayman was generally stronger in France and the UK, and in some cases in the US. Enlarging the reach of the IP, also towards Asia and performing well in the US, is the first ambition… making sure that we are a must-have platforming adventure title across those markets in the video game world.

“And I guess beyond the video game world. So, comics, TV series... actually, there’s a French comic book that came out with Rabbids and Rayman being reconnected.”

However, Gounon does not necessarily believe that producing a new 3D title is the key to success, and instead wants to focus on the characters and lore. Sorry to those hoping for Rayman 4 – hey, it might still happen!

“Rayman is iconic because of its gameplay. But going back to the adventure roots of Rayman, having people dive into those characters, exploring deeper into that world and mythology, that’s what we believe in.

“It’s the world-building part, the consistency of that world-building, and the empathy for those characters, that will make the franchise last and maybe become bigger.”

Rayman Legends Retold is right around the corner, scheduled to launch on 3rd December 2026. Meanwhile, Ubisoft itself is currently coming under fire for its heavy focus on generative AI, with a new report revealing that employees are required to justify reasons for not using the technology in new project pitches.

#4014. Crimson Desert PC specs don't keep resolution and framerate targets a secret, and they don't use upscaling for everything either

Finally, a PC specification list that actually indicates resolution and framerate targets, and doesn't leave console players behind.

Crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

It’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

#4013. Grand Theft Auto VI Reaches Highest Concurrent Player Count Ever For PS5, More than 683 Million Hours Logged Already

Grand Theft Auto VI hasn't even been out for a week, and it's already broken so many records that it's hard to keep up. It made $3.79 billion in just 24 hours after its November 19 launch, making it the biggest entertainment launch of all time. It comes as no surprise, then, that Rockstar Games' latest crime saga is also shattering records specifically on PlayStation 5.

In a new PlayStation Blog post, the company has revealed that more than 39 million unique players have booted up GTA VI on PS5, with the game setting a new record for the highest number of concurrent players for any game on PlayStation, surpassing previous records across multiplayer games such as Helldivers II, free-to-play games like Fortnite, and single-player releases like Elden Ring. What's more, PS5 players have already logged a cumulative 683 million hours of GTA VI gameplay – that's nearly 78,000 years' worth of time.

Other records for GTA VI on PS5 include the game giving PlayStation the "largest number of newly connected PS5 consoles on a single day since the console's launch, outside of end-of-year holidays," and GTA VI being the first game played on 70% of new PS5 consoles since the game's launch.

This is likely only the beginning of records GTA VI will continue to break.

#4010. Battlefield 6 is getting a free trial next week with a decent selection of maps and modes

Battlefield 6's second-ever free trial, and the first in 2026, is upon us.

Battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

Though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

For starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

Once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a big new update - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

#4009. Nioh 3 Comes To Xbox In January, Second Story DLC Launches Next Month

The Nioh series celebrates its 10th anniversary next February, and developer Team Ninja is celebrating with a pair of announcements for its latest entry, Nioh 3. First, the game's second story expansion, Bloody Insurrection, launches next month. Second, the game is coming to Xbox in January, marking the franchise's debut on Microsoft's platform.

Bloody Insurrection is Nioh 3's next story expansion following Hell Rising, which launched in August, and is set to release on December 18. Set in Shimabara in 1638, players will be at the center of a conflict between rebel forces, alchemists, and yokai while encountering familiar faces from previous Nioh games. Returning characters include Tachibana Muneshige from the original Nioh, and Bloody Insurrection will serve as the conclusion of protagonist Takechiyo's story.

Bloody Insurrection also introduces new Martial Arts for each weapon type, new Transformed Arts, Ninjutsu, Onmyo Magic, and Summoning Seals, and a new difficulty mode called Nioh's Journey. This new difficulty option is only available if you've completed the Enlightened One's Journey third playthrough and will allow players to find Ethereal equipment drops that let them acquire the highest rarity items in the game.

Additionally, Bloody Insurrection adds new endgame content called the Battlefield of Carnage. This challenges players with climbing floors, i.e., battlefields, filled with enemies and a boss. Each floor is divided into multiple battlefields, and defeating the floor's boss grants helpful battlefield effects, which can be combined to create unique synergies as you climb higher. Defeating enemies also lets players enhance special equipment "instilled with traces of the Yokai Realm," according to Koei Tecmo, which can only be found in Battlefield of Carnage.

A new edition of the game called Nioh 3: Complete Edition arrives on January 28 and will include the base game and its two story expansions. Complete Edition will arrive on PlayStation 5, PC, and, for the first time, Xbox Series X/S. The base version of Nioh 3 is also coming to Xbox Series X/S on the same date. The original version of Nioh 3 is also on sale at a 50 percent discount on PlayStation and Steam, and the season pass is 25 percent off.

For more on Nioh 3, be sure to read our review, in which we awarded the game a 9 out of 10. You can also check out our interview with Team Ninja discussing the Hell Rising expansion.

#4006. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.1 livestream reveals a pared-back, four-week update as HoYo plays catch-up

Honkai: Star Rail will continue the Planarcadia story arc in Version 4.1, as the Star Rail Fest presents a new twist.

A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major update. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the big focus of this update, in case it wasn't obvious.

The event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a new activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

Finally, Version 4.1 marks the start of a new Arcadian Chronicles phase in the Divergent Universe. You’ll be able to use Waypoint Pass cards to explore the different areas. HoYo is also bringing back Planar Fissure and Garden of Plenty with double rewards. And as ever, if you log in for at least seven days after downloading the new patch, you’ll earn 10 premium banner pulls.

#4005. Square Enix Says Its Efforts Supporting Switch 2 Have Contributed To Its Strong Financial Results

It's one of the platform's biggest third-party supporters

Square Enix has been one of the biggest third-party supporters of the Nintendo Switch 2, and it seems it's already paying off.

In the Japanese company's latest financial report, Square Enix president Takashi Kiryu has credited year-over-year net sales (¥11.6 billion to ¥35.6 billion) and operating income (¥8.0 billion to ¥13.0 billion) profits partly to its sales on Switch 2. Here's what he had to say:

Takashi Kiryu: "Efforts such as supporting new hardware, including the Nintendo Switch 2, and strengthening catalog title sales also contributed to our results. In the second half, in addition to FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, which launched on October 22, we plan to release DRAGON QUEST MONSTERS: The Withered World in December and Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United in February 2027. All are new titles, including remakes."

As touched on here by the president, Square Enix most recently released Final Fantasy Resonance on the Switch 2 and this will be followed by Dragon Quest Monsters: The Withered World in December and Romancing SaGa 3: Destinies United early next year.

This follows its release of games such as Dragon Quest VII: Reimagined, Kingdom Hearts Collection, Final Fantasy VII Rebirth and more this year. It's also released its MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV Online on Nintendo's hybrid platform in August, and next April sees the arrival of Final Fantasy VII Revelation.

Square left Nintendo development behind for a long time for a very good reason. Nintendo made some brain dead decisions in the mid 1990s that came back to haunt them. Mainly the fact that they never really lowered their licensing fees to compete with Sega and later Sony on that front. And secondly, using cartridges over CDs for the N64. Those two decisions is why Square went over to Sony for its primary development. And Yamauchi was a stick in the mud about it when Square tried to patch things up early after the switch.

But by the time the SE merger happened, Square and Nintendo both were willing to bury the hatchet. Square had already gotten over Yamauchi's nonsense and Nintendo was under new management and had finally dropped their licensing fees to be more in line with what Sony was doing. And the Gamecube was a complete 180 from what the N64 was development wise. The issue at that point came down mainly to business and sales expectations. Plus Sony pretty much provided the funding for their Worldwide releases outside of Japan. So those games weren't gonna go to Nintendo anyway. So SquareEnix went about curating exclusive games for Nintendo platforms that they felt wouldn't sell on Playstation anyway, with Nintendo doing a lot of the financial heavy lifting for areas outside of Japan (similar to what Sony had been doing since FFVII). The GBA games sold well, the GC game (Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles) didn't sell so well. Thus most Nintendo development over the next 15 years or so was focused primarily on their handhelds.

#4003. Be Careful, There's A Huge GTA 6 Spoiler Making The Rounds

Grand Theft Auto 6 was finally released over a week ago, so it's inevitable that spoilers are now hitting the internet.

However, achievement stats show that roughly 45% of players are still lapping it up in the keys with Brian and Donnie. There's plenty to do in the next few chapters that will keep people equally busy, so for those of you taking your time in Leonida and soaking in the sun at Vice Beach, be careful — there's a major spoiler making waves right now.

I'm still in Chapter 3, and have only just learned how to handle dye packs and rob banks, which I'm sure will keep me busy for another ten hours, so I haven't come across the spoiler myself, but there's a big reveal towards the end that people are now spamming in the comments or on subreddits without warning.

These posts get taken down pretty quickly in most cases, but if you're on the internet, it might be worth muting keywords, putting down TikTok, and avoiding the replies altogether.

I obviously won't discuss the spoiler here without warning, but it's a reveal that you won't want ruined.

If you're curious about what the spoiler is, or have already beaten the game, Niko Bellic makes an appearance in Grand Theft Auto 6 as "The Hitman."

People look back on GTA 4 with a lot more appreciation now, praising its weightier driving, mature storytelling, and how visceral the gunfights felt, but at launch, it quickly became the awkward middle child, and was widely criticized for cutting back on the systems in San Andreas. Thankfully, it's undergone something of a redemption in recent years as people are finally starting to appreciate GTA 4, even calling for a remaster. So, it's a real full-circle moment for Niko to return — especially considering Rockstar almost killed him off.

There's a tiny bit of dialogue in GTA 6 that you might've missed, hinting that Jason and Mandy might have some baggage.

Unfortunately, though, the internet is the internet, and spoiler posts are popping up on the GTA 4 subreddit without any labels, and viral GTA 6 posts on TikTok are almost always filled with comments about Niko. Facebook and Twitter are, as per, the worst offenders, with photos of him plastered in the replies.

Knowing that, maybe warn your friends to steer clear. I think we can all agree this is a reveal best appreciated firsthand.

The most anticipated video game of all time is a triumph on every level that exceeds years of unbelievable expectations. You're not ready for Leonida.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4002. Witchbrook Has Officially Gone Gold

The long-awaited cozy magical sim game Witchbrook has officially gone Gold, developer Chucklefish announced today. For those unfamiliar with the term “Gold," it generally means the game is complete and ready to be submitted to platforms for certification (and is less likely to be delayed).

Witchbrook is set to launch on January 28, ending a development cycle that stretches back nearly a decade. First teased in 2017, Witchbrook is a life-sim where players control a witch who begins life in the seaside town of Mossport. This includes making friends, finding love, and, most importantly, enrolling in Witchbrook College to master magic by taking classes and completing assignments.

We're delighted to announce that Witchbrook has GONE GOLD ALL PLATFORMS! 💛 We're can't for you all to join us on the journey on Jan 28th! ✨[image or embed]

Witchbrook is more or less Stardew Valley meets Hogwarts Legacy, as you can also start and run businesses, engage in seasonal events, and interact with fully fleshed-out citizens who have daily routines and schedules to consider. After a development cycle marked by long stretches of silence and several delays, those anticipating Witchbrook can breathe easier knowing the game will more than likely stick to its release date.

When Witchbrook launches on January 28, it will be available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Switch 2, Xbox One, Switch, and PC.

#4001. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.7 brings Angels of Delusion to the battlefield with playable Nangong Yu

Champions Never Fall to the Past indeed, as Zenless Zone Zero prepares for a major update that fans of Angels of Delusion will appreciate.

HoYoverse has delivered another Special Program for the second day running, this time for Zenless Zone Zero. The developer revealed the full details of Version 2.7, subtitled Champions Never Fall to the Past.

This next major update arrives March 24, adding two new Agents, and introducing the Hollow Champion competition.

Most things in Version 2.7 follow on from the Hollow Champion competition, which brings together old friends and familiar faces, as well interesting newcomers. Everyone is in it to win some big rewards and earn glory.

Among the unexpected participants the competition has attracted are the Public Security's Metropolitan Order Division, and even some former Calydon's Sweepers. A big challenge that awaits is Black Wolf Romeul, who’s capable of increasing his Crit Damage Resistance and Interruption Resistance by activating a Corruptive Barrier.

Romeul can also cause enemies to continuously lose HP, but you can beat him by putting together a squad that can deal sustained Anomaly damage, which will break through the barrier quickly.

Our first new arrival in Version 2.7 is Cissia of the Metropolitan Order Division. She is an S-Rank Electric Attack Agent who automatically gains three stacks of Venom when she enters the battle. Each stack deals Electric Damage while also increasing her Crit Rate for a time.

When she runs out of Venom, which will happen, Cissia can generate more stacks by using her EX Special Attack. She can also use her Basic Attack, Serpent's Kiss, to better utilise the new stacks of Venom she generates.

The other new Agent may be the more exciting. Nangong Yu, the captain and lead dancer of the Angels of Delusion, can now be part of your team. Nangong Yu is an S-Rank Ether Stun Agent who can boost her team’s Anomaly Buildup Rate against Stunned enemies.

Being part of an idol group has its perks, because she automatically regenerates Downbeat as time goes on, and even more any time a squad member inflicts an enemy with Anomaly. Nangong Yu can then use Downbeat - after enough has been accumulated - on charged attacks that keep enemies stunned for longer. Her Ultimate triggers Ether Veil: Delusion Reprise, which boosts the entire squad’s Attack.

Returning Agents in Version 2.7 will be Yidhari, the S-Rank Ice Rupture Agent, as well as Seed, the Electric Attack Agent.

Outside of all the very important action in the core story, this chapter also brings new themed events to Lumina Square’s Simmer Hot Pot Restaurant. The Simulated Battle Trial is also getting some love, with updated mechanics and new enemy line-ups.

Catch up on our recently updated Zenless Zone Zero character tier list, and don’t forget to check out these Zenless Zone Zero codes before you jump in for some free stuff.

#4000. Jupiter's Picross Series For Switch Has Officially Surpassed One Million Sales

The first title released on the eShop in 2017

If you've ever bought one of Jupiter Corporation's Picross games on the Switch, you've helped the series reach a major milestone.

The Kyoto-based developer has this week announced its Picross series for Switch has now surpassed one million downloads. Since the launch of Picross S on the Switch in 2017, Jupiter has gone on to release more than 20 Picross titles (including all sorts of crossovers).

Earlier this year in March, we saw the release of the Picross S Konami Antiques Edition, which featured popular Konami IP such as Castlevania and Contra. The news of one million sales this week happens to be taking place ahead of the release of the new game Picross S Climax.

Picross S Climax launches on the Japanese eShop on 10th December 2026. To help build some excitement, Jupiter has released a demo for the new title. There'll also be a series sale taking place on 30th November 2026, with the Konami Antiques Edition going on sale for the first time and Picross S 50% off.

Jupiter's history with the Picross video games stretches way back to the Super Nintendo and Game Boy era, with titles such as Mario's Super Picross and Mario's Picross. These games can now be accessed via the Switch Online 'Nintendo Classics' service.

#3999. I Hate Video Game Romance – Here's Why Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Exception

Generally speaking, I do not like romance mechanics in video games. I never find them convincing. Relationships build way too quickly, and usually all it takes to win someone over in an RPG or farming sim is a couple of conversations and a few gifts. In Grand Theft Auto VI, however, I'm extremely invested in the romance between Jason and Lucia, and it comes down to the game's quieter moments and slice-of-life mechanics.

If you've played Baldur's Gate 3, Stardew Valley, Date Everything, or practically any other game with romance options, you're familiar with the gameplay loop. I ask an NPC about her hometown, sympathize with her tragic backstory, promise to be there for her, and then give her the book, cake, or mining resource she likes. Do it enough, and one day she'll approach me with the uncharacteristically heartfelt confession that she can't stop thinking about me. The process is too transparently mechanical: I can scan the dialogue options and instantly know which of the three sentences will boost my affinity rating the most. It feels less like an actual relationship and more like a long-term scheme to program someone into dating.

Many games structured like the ones above are written as well as they can be. The issue is scope and structure. Romantic relationships are nuanced and unique, but there often aren't enough resources during a game's development to represent more than the basic building blocks. Players are meant to suspend disbelief and fill in the gaps – even though you technically only spoke to that villager a few dozen times, you're married with a child, so you imagine it's actually been years.

Of course, this scope is the difference between Grand Theft Auto VI and these other games – Rockstar made time and space for everything in this world, and romance is no exception.

Since they're dating when the game begins, Jason and Lucia admittedly skip the courtship phase that many games focus on, but their relationship is still conditional and malleable – if you want them to like each other, you should be acting in their best interests. And while the mechanical aspect of their romance is still plenty visible, the actions to increase that meter are vastly expanded. There has been a lot of discussion about the early game, when you can prep for Lucia's release from prison by buying flowers or groceries, and while I like those gestures, they're not what sold me on the relationship. Say what you will about modern dating standards, but flowers and food are too easy – too obvious for me to feel connected to and invested in a couple.

When I played this section, I felt like Jason's hair looked a little unkempt, so I got a shave and a haircut. And, to my surprise, this improved his relationship with Lucia. She wasn't around and wouldn't see the results until later, but it still scored me partner points, as did repairing the roof, painting the bedroom walls, and even giving Jason's car a new paint job. These unexpected, specific tasks don't just fill up the relationship gauge – they communicate information about both characters. Lucia is really looking forward to getting out of prison, and having a finished house and a clean, put-together partner sets her in a better mood. Meanwhile, my actions establish that my version of Jason knows she likes these things and would do them without even asking.

Minor, specific tasks like these are romantic because they imply a degree of thoughtfulness that sidesteps the grand gestures expected of a long-awaited reunion. Yes, there should be apples in the fridge, but that's a basic need; knowing the exact conditions Lucia wants the house to be in makes me believe Jason actually knows her. It becomes even more effective – both in real relationships and in the credibility of the in-game partnership – when thoughtfulness is demonstrated on a day-to-day basis, in the quiet moments.

Grand Theft Auto VI is a long game with a slow, steady pace, leaving room for the intimate interactions other games wouldn't have time for. If you come home at the end of the day and see your partner watching TV, you can sit next to them and get a bonus. When they go to sleep, they'll call out to you and ask you to lie in bed and scroll on your phone with them. You can hold hands in public, buy each other clothes, and remember to text back promptly. There are large, dramatic moments and professions of love, yes, but players are likely to experience vastly more of these minor interactions than those scripted cutscenes.

Romance can be flashy, but it has to be more than that. It's nice to see the starring duo dance, drive, and shoot at foes during cutscenes. But it's the long car rides when Lucia reassures Jason that her mom likes him, or the evening on the couch when Jason talks about how he likes the way Lucia laughs, that make this relationship work narratively.

What are your favorite video game romances? Let us know in the comments!

#3998. Heartopia goes to the movies with its next event

Heartopia's Whale Island will soon host a new event that's all about the magic of cinema.

Heartopia’s next in-game event has been announced, and it’s one you may not have seen coming. Developer XD Games revealed Dreamlight Cinematics Festival, an upcoming limited-time event that celebrates cinema and movie-making.

Dreamlight Cinematics kicks off March 21, and will run through May 1, available across the game’s PC and mobile versions.

Dreamlight Cinematics Festival takes place on Whale Island. And, perhaps as an unofficial Oscars tie-in, it’s all about classic Hollywood filmmaking. Not only that, it also celebrates the aesthetics and industrial design of that era.

All around the game’s world, you’ll be able to find festival-themed collectables, which you can then use to unlock free Time-Limited Exhibition Passes.

If you log in during the event’s runtime, you’ll get the Car Cinema furniture set for free. This cosmetic bundle comes with chairs that are modelled after vintage vehicles, as well as poster display stands with unique movie making-themed decorations.

If you’re looking to spend some money, the Deluxe Festival Pack comes with a large Island Sunset Billboard, which you can place outside your home so everyone knows you spent that money. The same pack also comes with the Popcorn Movie Ticket chat bubble skin, and a 10% bonus to Festival Tokens when you sell stuff at the store.

Regardless of which pack you get, you’ll earn collection points for each, which puts you on the path to unlocking outfits like the Dreamlight Cinematics Festival-specific Modern Show Dandy and Modern Show Belle. There’s also a Cinematic Moments building material set launching with this event.

For now, we have the above reveal trailer to go on, which does offer some idea of what it’s going to look like in-game. Until things kick off on the weekend, you best arm yourself with some Heartopia codes.
